title: EyeRobot 2.0: Active Gaze for Precise Manipulation without Wrist Cameras
why_read: A robotics paper showing that an active, foveated stereo-camera gaze system can match or beat wrist-camera setups, which is a meaningful hardware-simplification result for manipulation research.
analysis: EyeRobot 2.0 uses two actively steerable cameras that physically point toward a 3D fixation point, mimicking human eye movements, instead of relying on a camera mounted on the robot's wrist. The system is trained hierarchically: one policy learns to aim the gaze at a goal object, and another learns when to shift fixation based on task progress, both using reinforcement learning on real robot data. Across over a thousand real and simulated trials, this approach substantially closes the performance gap with wrist-camera policies and even outperforms them when the object blocks the wrist camera's view, which is a notable practical finding for manipulation system design.
